solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trading establishments with wages about right in one part of England

indicators.note: the shop-and-wages pair is placed about, i.e. around, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: shops are places where trade is done
hire is an old word for payment for work, as in 'the labourer is worthy of his hire'

explanation.surface: A complaint that shops in some English region pay wages that are only just about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside SHOPSHIRE, after the SH. SHROPSHIRE is a county in the West Midlands of England, on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Shropshire is a county, which is literally one region of England.

clue.text: Hebrew character unhappy over Exile primarily

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, i.e. above, the second

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the word Exile

explanation.surface: A Jewish figure is miserable about being in exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Sade (or tsade) is a letter of the Hebrew alphabet, and a character can mean a written letter.

clue.text: Artist needing help, a troubled painter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of these words are stirred up

explanation.surface: An artist in difficulties needs assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' is RA, a Royal Academician, a crossword staple; 'troubled' yields PHAEL. 'Artist' looks like the definition, but the painter is at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was the great Italian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Owner given support tries altering outside of residence, somewhat cut off

parts.note: a prop is something that supports

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go outside, i.e. around, the shortened word
altering means changing, so the letters of tries are rearranged
residence is cut off a good deal, leaving only its first three letters

explanation.surface: An owner, backed up, attempts to change the exterior of a house that is rather isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' makes RIETS, which sits 'outside of' residence 'somewhat cut off', its first three letters; 'outside' reads like the house's exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietress is a female proprietor, a woman who owns a business or property.

clue.text: More enthusiastic Italian standing up is grabbed by one in the audience

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation is held inside the listener's word

parts.note: a hearer is someone listening, a member of an audience

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian on his feet is collared by a keener member of the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' reverses IT to TI, which 'is grabbed by' HEARER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means warm and enthusiastic, so the comparative form is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Group of soldiers willingly supplying help to the poor

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly, as in 'I'd as lief'

explanation.surface: A unit of troops gladly handing out aid to the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor relief was the historical name for public assistance given to the destitute.

clue.text: Badger meeting a snake

parts.note: to badger someone is to nag them

explanation.surface: A badger and a snake encounter each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Naga is a cobra in Indian usage, and also a serpent being of Hindu myth.

clue.text: Man in garden, worker for firm

parts.note: Adam was the first man, in the Garden of Eden
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A gardener is described as a labourer for a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, resolute, firm in one's position.

clue.text: An undertaking to clad home in glass

indicators.note: to clad is to cover, so the enterprise word wraps around the home word

parts.note: a venture is an undertaking or enterprise
in means at home

explanation.surface: A building project sheathing a house in glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home' is IN as in 'at home', and 'to clad' wraps the undertaking around it. 'glass' is a specific decorative glass, not a generic.
explanation.definitionFit: Aventurine is a kind of glass flecked with copper particles that sparkle, also a similar quartz.

clue.text: Delightful leader emerging outside Eastern place providing base

indicators.note: the shortened word goes outside, i.e. around, the two abbreviations
the leading letter comes out of the delightful word

parts.note: adorable means delightful
PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses

explanation.surface: A charming leader comes out of an Eastern place that offers a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader emerging' takes A off ADORABLE to give DORABLE, which goes 'outside' E and PL. 'base' is the adjective meaning low, not a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Base meaning morally low or contemptible is a synonym of deplorable.

clue.text: Youngster makes confused sound endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly removes the last letter of the word

parts.note: babel is a confused noise of many voices, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: A child produces a garbled noise without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final L from BABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is a baby or young child.

clue.text: Rioters come on the rampage, blocking entrance to reactor — such violence?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters block, i.e. surround, the single letter
rioters running wild means the letters of these two words are thrown about
entrance to takes the first letter of reactor

explanation.surface: A riot mob storms a nuclear plant, cutting off access: is that what such violence would be called?
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' rearranges RIOTERSCOME, and these letters are 'blocking' R, the 'entrance to reactor'. The question mark marks the definition as an example drawn from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecoterrorism is violence or sabotage carried out in the name of environmental causes, such as attacking a nuclear plant.

clue.text: Market price being announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a fare is the price of a journey

explanation.surface: A market price is being declared.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair is a periodic gathering for trading goods and livestock, a market.

clue.text: Keen wind almost getting to sing

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: to trend is to bend or turn in a direction, as a road or river winds
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A sharp wind nearly makes one start singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts TREND to TREN. 'Keen' looks like it describes the wind but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen in the sense of sharp or incisive, as of a blade or wit, is a synonym.

clue.text: Character among thieves finds devices for entering rooms maybe

indicators.note: among puts the character word inside the thieving word

parts.note: to thieve is to steal or swipe, so thieves (verb) means swipes
a card is an eccentric character

explanation.surface: A figure in a gang of burglars discovers tools for breaking into rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thieves' looks like a plural noun but is a verb, steals. 'maybe' marks rooms as one example of what the devices open.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipe cards are plastic key cards passed through a reader to unlock doors, as in hotels.

clue.text: We had to go round passageway squinting

indicators.note: the contraction goes around the passage word

parts.note: WE'D is the contraction of we had
an alley is a narrow passageway

explanation.surface: We were obliged to walk around a passage while peering.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall-eyed describes eyes that turn outward, a kind of squint.

clue.text: Mechanical device turns around, expending energy

indicators.note: expending means using up, so a letter is lost
around means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: turns means rotates
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A machine spins around, using up power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses ROTATES to SETATOR; 'expending energy' removes an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stator is the stationary part of a motor or generator, within which the rotor turns.

clue.text: Good essayist enthralled by female follower of philosopher

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so the pair goes inside

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A fine writer of essays is captivated by a woman who follows a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' places good and the essayist inside the female; Elia was Charles Lamb's pen name, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hegelian is a disciple of the German philosopher Hegel.

clue.text: It's mean putting chum to test

parts.note: a chum is a pal, a friend
to try is to test

explanation.surface: It is unkind to put a friend through a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like unkind, but here it is the sense of meagre.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of small or meagre, as in no mean feat, matches trifling.

clue.text: Roman god looks down on monarch having fun

indicators.note: in a down clue the god sits above the monarch, so comes first

parts.note: a Lar was a Roman household god
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A Roman deity views a king with contempt while amusing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to play pranks and enjoy oneself, so larking means fooling around.

clue.text: Animal wanting ground to keep soft

indicators.note: the land word keeps, i.e. holds, the soft letter inside

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A creature needs land in order to stay gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle, an animal.

clue.text: Prohibition-buster has drinks provided outside gates

indicators.note: the drinks go outside, around, the gangster

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, so ports are drinks
Al Capone was the gangster who flouted Prohibition in 1920s America

explanation.surface: A bootlegger has liquor brought out to the gates.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, made his fortune defying Prohibition; 'outside' wraps the drinks around his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Portals are grand doorways or gates.

clue.text: Permit gets vehicle free from all charges

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
net means after all deductions

explanation.surface: A permit lets a car go without paying any fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnet is a customs document or licence permitting goods or vehicles across borders.

clue.text: Sparkle as American chap in central part

indicators.note: the two pieces go in the centre word

parts.note: the core is the central part
US means American
cat is slang for a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: An American guy shines at the heart of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to flash or glitter, a synonym of sparkle.

clue.text: Soup component cook rarely uses

indicators.note: uses means the words employ the letters within them

explanation.surface: A cook seldom puts something in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra is a pod vegetable used to thicken soups such as gumbo.

clue.text: Bird in number crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the number goes round the letter

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A bird among many that fly over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain category membership: the tern is a slender, fork-tailed seabird related to the gull.

clue.text: Bird that's poorly hiding head

indicators.note: hiding the head drops the first letter

parts.note: poorly means unwell or frail

explanation.surface: An ailing bird tucks its head away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a marsh bird, related to the coot.

clue.text: Girl knocked over, having been hemmed in by close cow

indicators.note: the girl is enclosed inside the close word

parts.note: intimate means close

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Di is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is knocked flat by a cow pressing on her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns the girl's name backwards to ID. 'cow' looks like the animal but is the verb, to frighten into submission.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow is to frighten into submission.

clue.text: With time passing, great number sound regretful

indicators.note: passing means going away, so a letter goes

parts.note: a sight is informally a great deal, as in a sight more

explanation.surface: As time goes by, many people express their sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh is to breathe out audibly in sadness or regret.

clue.text: Man soon set out to be skilled worker

indicators.note: set out signals the letters are laid out anew; out means disordered

explanation.surface: A man will soon go off and become a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a craftsman trained to cut and lay stone.
